name: Avocado Toast with Poached Eggs
instructions: Toast bread slices until golden and crispy.
Mash avocado with lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Rub toast with a halved garlic clove while warm.
Spread mashed avocado generously on toast.
For poached eggs: bring water to a gentle simmer with a splash of vinegar.
Create a gentle swirl in water, crack egg into center.
Poach for 3-4 minutes until white is set but yolk is runny.
Place poached egg on avocado toast, drizzle with olive oil, add red pepper flakes.
cooking_tips: Add vinegar to poaching water to help whites hold together.
Fresh eggs poach better than older eggs.
Add everything bagel seasoning for extra flavor.
serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with a side of fresh fruit or a small green salad.
storage_tips: Best eaten immediately. Avocado browns quickly when exposed to air.

name: Masala Omelette
instructions: Beat eggs well with salt and a pinch of turmeric.
Add finely chopped onion, tomato, green chili, and coriander.
Mix everything together.
Heat butter in a pan over medium heat.
Pour egg mixture into the pan, spreading evenly.
Let cook undisturbed for 2 minutes until bottom is set.
Fold omelette in half and cook for 1 more minute.
Serve hot with toast or bread.
cooking_tips: Beat eggs properly for a fluffy omelette.
Don't overfill — the omelette won't fold properly.
Medium heat prevents rubbery eggs.
serving_suggestions: Serve with buttered toast and masala chai.
storage_tips: Best eaten immediately. Eggs get rubbery when reheated.

name: Overnight Oats
instructions: In a mason jar or bowl, combine rolled oats and chia seeds.
Add milk and yogurt. Mix well.
Add vanilla extract, cinnamon, and honey.
Stir until everything is well combined.
Top with sliced banana and berries.
Cover and refrigerate overnight (at least 6 hours).
In the morning, stir and add a little milk if too thick.
Add fresh toppings and enjoy cold or warmed up.
cooking_tips: Use at least a 1:1.5 ratio of oats to liquid.
Steel-cut oats need 24 hours soaking time.
Add toppings fresh in the morning for best texture.
serving_suggestions: Serve cold in summer or warm in winter. Top with nut butter for extra protein.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for up to 5 days without toppings.

substitutions.milk: almond milk, oat milk, or coconut milk

name: Poha (Flattened Rice Breakfast)
instructions: Wash poha gently and drain. Let sit for 5 minutes until softened.
Season with salt, turmeric, and a pinch of sugar. Set aside.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Add peanuts and fry until golden.
Add curry leaves, green chili, and onions. Cook until soft.
Add diced potato and cook covered for 5 minutes.
Add the seasoned poha and mix gently.
Cook covered for 3-4 minutes. Finish with lemon juice and coriander.
cooking_tips: Don't over-soak poha — it should be just softened, not mushy.
Use thick poha for best texture.
The sugar balances the sour-spicy flavors.
serving_suggestions: Serve hot with coconut chutney and a cup of chai.
storage_tips: Best eaten fresh. Can be refrigerated for 1 day.

name: French Toast
instructions: Beat eggs with milk, cinnamon, vanilla extract, and sugar.
Heat butter in a pan over medium heat.
Dip bread slices in egg mixture, coating both sides.
Place soaked bread in the pan.
Cook 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Repeat for remaining bread slices.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve with maple syrup.
Add fresh berries or sliced banana on the side.
cooking_tips: Use day-old or slightly stale bread — it absorbs better.
Thick-cut brioche or challah makes the best French toast.
Medium heat prevents burning while cooking through.
serving_suggestions: Serve with maple syrup, fresh berries, and whipped cream.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for 2 days. Reheat in a pan or toaster.

name: Kung Pao Chicken
instructions: Cut chicken into bite-sized cubes. Marinate with soy sauce and cornstarch.
Mix sauce: soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, and cornstarch.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Stir-fry dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns for 30 seconds.
Add marinated chicken and cook until golden.
Add garlic and ginger, stir-fry for 1 minute.
Pour in sauce mixture and toss to coat.
Add peanuts and green onions, toss and serve immediately.
cooking_tips: High heat is essential for proper wok cooking.
Have all ingredients prepped before starting — it cooks fast.
Toast peanuts beforehand for better flavor.
serving_suggestions: Serve over steamed white rice or fried rice.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for up to 2 days. Best eaten fresh.

name: Egg Fried Rice
instructions: Use day-old cold rice for best results.
Beat eggs with a pinch of salt.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Scramble eggs in the wok, break into small pieces, set aside.
Add more oil, stir-fry garlic and onions until fragrant.
Add cold rice and stir-fry vigorously, breaking up any clumps.
Add scrambled eggs back and toss together.
Season with soy sauce, white pepper, and sesame oil. Top with green onions.
cooking_tips: Cold, day-old rice is key — fresh rice gets mushy.
Cook on very high heat for the 'wok hei' smoky flavor.
Keep everything moving in the wok.
serving_suggestions: Serve as a main dish or as a side with other Chinese dishes.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat in a hot wok.

name: Sweet and Sour Pork
instructions: Cut pork into chunks, marinate with soy sauce for 15 minutes.
Coat pork pieces in egg then cornstarch.
Deep fry pork until golden and crispy. Set aside.
Make sauce: mix ketchup, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, and water.
Stir-fry onions, bell peppers, and pineapple for 2 minutes.
Add sauce and bring to a boil.
Add fried pork and toss to coat.
Thicken with cornstarch slurry if needed.
cooking_tips: Double frying pork makes it extra crispy.
Add pork at the last minute to keep it crispy.
Fresh pineapple gives better flavor than canned.
serving_suggestions: Serve over steamed rice with a garnish of sesame seeds.
storage_tips: Store sauce and pork separately. Combine when serving.

substitutions.ketchup: tomato paste with extra vinegar and sugar

name: Mapo Tofu
instructions: Cut tofu into 1-inch cubes. Blanch in salted water for 2 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok, fry garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add chili bean paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add vegetable broth and bring to simmer.
Gently add tofu and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add soy sauce and sesame oil.
Thicken with cornstarch slurry.
Garnish with Sichuan pepper and green onions.
cooking_tips: Silken tofu is traditional but firm tofu holds up better.
Blanching tofu removes any bitterness.
Sichuan peppercorns give the characteristic numbing sensation.
serving_suggestions: Serve over steamed rice. The spicy sauce is perfect for soaking up.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for 2 days but tofu softens over time.

name: Spring Rolls
instructions: Shred cabbage and carrots, slice mushrooms thin.
Stir-fry vegetables with garlic and ginger until softened.
Season with soy sauce and sesame oil. Let cool completely.
Place filling on spring roll wrapper diagonally.
Fold in sides, roll tightly, seal edge with cornstarch paste.
Heat oil to 175°C for deep frying.
Fry spring rolls in batches until golden and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.
cooking_tips: Let filling cool completely before rolling to prevent soggy wrappers.
Make sure oil is hot enough before frying.
For baked version, brush with oil and bake at 200°C.
serving_suggestions: Serve with sweet chili sauce or soy dipping sauce.
storage_tips: Freeze uncooked rolls for up to 2 months. Fry from frozen.

name: Chocolate Lava Cake
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C. Grease ramekins with butter and dust with cocoa powder.
Melt dark chocolate and butter together in a double boiler or microwave.
Whisk eggs, egg yolks, and sugar until pale and doubled in volume.
Fold melted chocolate mixture into egg mixture.
Gently fold in flour and salt until just combined.
Pour batter into prepared ramekins, fill 3/4 full.
Bake for 10-12 minutes — center should be slightly wobbly.
Let rest 1 minute, then carefully invert onto plates. Serve immediately.
cooking_tips: The key is underbaking — the center should be liquid.
You can refrigerate the batter for up to 24 hours before baking.
Use high quality dark chocolate (70%+) for best results.
serving_suggestions: Serve with vanilla ice cream, fresh berries, or a dusting of powdered sugar.
storage_tips: Batter can be stored in ramekins in fridge for 24 hours unbaked.

name: Classic Tiramisu
instructions: Brew strong espresso, let cool completely, add rum if using.
Separate eggs. Beat yolks with sugar until pale and thick.
Fold mascarpone cheese into egg yolk mixture until smooth.
Beat egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold into mascarpone mixture.
Quickly dip ladyfingers in espresso and layer in a dish.
Spread half the mascarpone cream over the ladyfingers.
Add another layer of soaked ladyfingers and top with remaining cream.
Dust generously with cocoa powder and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
cooking_tips: Don't over-soak ladyfingers — a quick dip is enough.
Overnight refrigeration gives the best flavor.
Use room temperature mascarpone for smooth mixing.
serving_suggestions: Serve chilled directly from the dish. Garnish with chocolate shavings.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for up to 3 days. The flavor actually improves overnight.

name: Mango Kulfi
instructions: Warm 2 tablespoons of cream and dissolve saffron in it.
In a bowl, mix mango puree and condensed milk.
Whip remaining heavy cream to soft peaks.
Fold whipped cream into mango mixture.
Add cardamom powder, saffron cream, and rose water.
Pour into kulfi molds or popsicle molds.
Sprinkle chopped pistachios on top.
Freeze for at least 6 hours or overnight.
cooking_tips: Use ripe Alphonso mangoes for authentic flavor.
The condensed milk adds sweetness — no extra sugar needed.
Unmold by briefly running warm water over the outside.
serving_suggestions: Serve garnished with chopped pistachios and rose petals.
storage_tips: Store in freezer for up to 1 month.

substitutions.mango: strawberry puree or any fruit puree

name: Banana Foster Pancakes
instructions: Mash 1 ripe banana and mix with egg, milk, and melted butter.
Combine flour, baking powder, sugar, cinnamon, and salt.
Mix wet and dry ingredients until just combined — lumps are okay.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat, lightly grease.
Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake. Cook until bubbles form, flip.
For the banana foster sauce: melt butter, add brown sugar and cinnamon.
Add sliced bananas and cook for 2 minutes.
Serve pancakes topped with warm banana foster sauce.
cooking_tips: Overripe bananas make the sweetest pancakes.
Don't overmix the batter — lumps give fluffy pancakes.
Medium heat prevents burning while cooking through.
serving_suggestions: Serve with maple syrup, whipped cream, and a sprinkle of cinnamon.
storage_tips: Pancakes keep in fridge for 2 days. Reheat in a pan or toaster.

substitutions.egg: flax egg (1 tbsp flaxseed + 3 tbsp water)

name: Gulab Jamun
instructions: Make sugar syrup: boil sugar, water, cardamom, and saffron. Add rose water.
Combine milk powder, flour, and baking soda.
Rub in ghee until mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Add milk gradually to form a soft, smooth dough.
Rest dough for 10 minutes. Shape into smooth balls.
Heat oil on low-medium heat. Fry gulab jamuns slowly until dark golden.
Immediately drop hot gulab jamuns into warm sugar syrup.
Soak for at least 30 minutes before serving.
cooking_tips: Fry on low heat — the inside must cook through before outside burns.
Warm sugar syrup absorbs better into hot gulab jamuns.
Make balls smooth with no cracks to prevent breaking.
serving_suggestions: Serve warm with vanilla ice cream or rabri.
storage_tips: Store in syrup at room temperature for 2 days or refrigerate for 1 week.

name: Savory Mushroom Oatmeal
instructions: Heat olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Sauté chopped onion and garlic until translucent.
Add sliced mushrooms and cook until browned.
Stir in rolled oats and thyme for 1 minute.
Pour in vegetable broth and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add spinach and cook until wilted.
Season with salt and pepper, then stir in Parmesan cheese.
Divide into bowls and finish with extra black pepper.
cooking_tips: Use gluten-free oats if needed.
Keep stirring to prevent the oats from sticking.
Add a splash of cream or milk if you prefer a creamier texture.
serving_suggestions: Top with fresh herbs or a poached egg for a richer meal.
storage_tips: Store refrigerated for up to 2 days and reheat with a little broth.

name: Chana Masala
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds until they crackle.
Add chopped onion and cook until golden.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, coriander powder, and cook until oil separates.
Add chickpeas, salt, and a little water. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in garam masala and chopped green chili.
Cook for 5 more minutes and garnish with cilantro.
Serve hot with rice or flatbread.
cooking_tips: Use canned chickpeas for a quick version.
Toast your spices briefly to release fuller flavor.
Adjust chili and lemon to taste for a balanced finish.
serving_suggestions: Pair with basmati rice, naan, or a cucumber raita.
storage_tips: Store in the fridge for 3 days; flavors deepen overnight.

name: Lemon Herb Salmon
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Place salmon fillets on a baking sheet lined with parchment.
Drizzle olive oil and lemon juice over the salmon.
Sprinkle minced garlic, chopped herbs, salt, and pepper.
Bake for 12-15 minutes until salmon flakes easily.
Remove from oven and let rest for 2 minutes.
Serve with extra lemon wedges and fresh herbs.
cooking_tips: Do not overcook — salmon should still be moist inside.
Use fresh lemon for the brightest flavor.
Baking on parchment makes cleanup easier.
serving_suggestions: Serve with roasted vegetables and a simple salad.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for 2 days and reheat gently to avoid drying out.

name: Caprese Salad
instructions: Slice tomatoes and fresh mozzarella into even rounds.
Arrange tomato and mozzarella slices alternately on a platter.
Tuck basil leaves between the layers.
Drizzle with olive oil and balsamic glaze.
Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Serve immediately at room temperature.
cooking_tips: Use the ripest tomatoes for the best flavor.
Let mozzarella come to room temperature before serving.
A splash of basil oil enhances the dish.
serving_suggestions: Serve as an appetizer with crusty bread.
storage_tips: Best eaten immediately. If storing, keep chilled and consume within a few hours.

name: Vegan Black Bean Tacos
instructions: Heat olive oil in a pan and sauté chopped onion and garlic.
Add black beans, cumin, chili powder, salt, and a splash of water.
Simmer for 8-10 minutes until warmed through.
Mash some of the beans lightly to thicken the mixture.
Warm taco shells according to package instructions.
Fill shells with black bean mixture, lettuce, tomato, avocado, and cilantro.
Squeeze lime juice over the tacos before serving.
cooking_tips: Use low-sodium beans and add salt to taste.
For extra smokiness, add a dash of smoked paprika.
Crisp the shells in the oven for a better texture.
serving_suggestions: Serve with salsa, guacamole, and pickled onions.
storage_tips: Store bean filling separately from shells for up to 3 days.

name: Shrimp Pad Thai
instructions: Soak rice noodles according to package directions until pliable.
Mix tamarind paste, fish sauce, brown sugar, and lime juice in a bowl.
Heat oil in a wok, sauté garlic until fragrant.
Add shrimp and cook until pink, then push to the side.
Crack egg into the wok and scramble until just set.
Add drained noodles and sauce, tossing to coat.
Stir in bean sprouts and green onion, cook for 1-2 minutes.
Serve topped with chopped peanuts and lime wedges.
cooking_tips: Work quickly once the noodles are in the wok.
Use room-temperature shrimp for even cooking.
Adjust sweetness and sourness by tasting the sauce.
serving_suggestions: Serve with extra lime wedges and cilantro.
storage_tips: Eat fresh. Reheat gently if needed, but noodles may soften.

name: Chocolate Chia Pudding
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together almond milk, cocoa powder, maple syrup, and vanilla.
Stir in chia seeds until evenly distributed.
Let the mixture sit for 5 minutes, then stir again to prevent clumps.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 3 hours or overnight.
Stir again before serving and top with sliced banana and berries.
Serve chilled.
cooking_tips: Use fresh chia seeds and whisk well to avoid clumping.
Add a dollop of nut butter for extra richness.
The pudding thickens as it chills — thin with extra milk if needed.
serving_suggestions: Top with nuts, shredded coconut, or fresh fruit.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for up to 4 days.

name: Spinach Strawberry Salad
instructions: Toss baby spinach, sliced strawberries, and thinly sliced red onion in a bowl.
Add crumbled goat cheese and chopped walnuts.
Whisk together balsamic vinegar, olive oil, honey, salt, and pepper.
Pour dressing over the salad and toss gently.
Serve immediately as a fresh side dish.
cooking_tips: Use ripe strawberries for the sweetest flavor.
Toast walnuts lightly for extra crunch.
Dress the salad just before serving to avoid sogginess.
serving_suggestions: Serve alongside grilled chicken or fish.
storage_tips: Prepare components separately and toss before serving.

name: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
instructions: Marinate chicken in yogurt, turmeric, chili powder, and salt for at least 1 hour.
Heat oil in a pan and cook marinated chicken until golden brown. Set aside.
In the same pan, melt butter and sauté onions until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add tomato puree, garam masala, cumin, coriander, and cook for 10 minutes.
Blend the sauce until smooth, then return to pan.
Add cooked chicken and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in cream, adjust seasoning, and garnish with fresh coriander.
cooking_tips: Marinate chicken overnight for deeper flavor.
Use kasuri methi (dried fenugreek) for authentic taste.
Blend the sauce for a silky smooth texture.
serving_suggestions: Serve hot with naan bread, basmati rice, or roti. Garnish with a swirl of cream.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 1 month.

substitutions.chicken: paneer or tofu for vegetarian version

name: Dal Tadka
instructions: Wash and soak yellow lentils for 20 minutes.
Pressure cook lentils with turmeric and salt until soft.
Heat ghee in a pan, add mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Add cumin, dried red chili, and garlic. Sauté until golden.
Add onions and cook until translucent.
Add tomatoes, ginger and cook until oil separates.
Pour this tadka over cooked lentils and stir well.
Garnish with fresh coriander and a squeeze of lemon.
cooking_tips: Soaking lentils reduces cooking time significantly.
The tadka (tempering) is the key to this dish's flavor.
Add a pinch of asafoetida for authentic taste.
serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed basmati rice or jeera rice. Perfect with roti.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for up to 4 days. Add water when reheating as it thickens.

name: Palak Paneer
instructions: Blanch spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes, then immediately transfer to cold water.
Blend blanched spinach into a smooth puree.
Heat butter in a pan, fry cubed paneer until golden on all sides. Set aside.
In the same pan, add cumin seeds, then onions and cook until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes, and all spices. Cook until oil separates.
Add spinach puree and cook for 5 minutes.
Add fried paneer and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Stir in cream, season with salt and serve hot.
cooking_tips: Blanch and immediately cool spinach to retain its vibrant green color.
Frying paneer gives it a nice texture that holds up in the curry.
Do not overcook spinach as it turns dark.
serving_suggestions: Serve with butter naan, tandoori roti, or jeera rice.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for 2-3 days. The color may darken but taste remains good.

name: Chicken Biryani
instructions: Marinate chicken with yogurt, biryani masala, ginger-garlic paste for 2 hours.
Parboil basmati rice with whole spices until 70% cooked. Drain.
Fry sliced onions until deep golden brown (birista). Set aside.
Cook marinated chicken in a heavy pan until half done.
Layer parboiled rice over chicken.
Add saffron milk, fried onions, mint leaves, and ghee on top.
Seal the pot with dough or foil and cook on low heat (dum) for 25 minutes.
Gently mix from bottom before serving.
cooking_tips: The dum (slow steam cooking) is what makes biryani special.
Crispy golden onions add essential flavor and texture.
Soak rice for 30 minutes before parboiling.
serving_suggestions: Serve with raita, mirchi ka salan, and papad.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for 2 days. Reheat with a sprinkle of water to prevent drying.

name: Aloo Gobi
instructions: Cut potatoes into cubes and cauliflower into small florets.
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add onions and cook until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and all spices, cook until oil separates.
Add potatoes, mix well, and cook covered for 10 minutes.
Add cauliflower and continue cooking until both vegetables are tender.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot.
cooking_tips: Don't add water — let vegetables cook in their own moisture.
Parboiling potatoes can reduce cooking time.
Add amchur (dry mango powder) for tangy flavor.
serving_suggestions: Serve with roti, paratha, or as a side dish with dal and rice.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for 2-3 days. Best when freshly made.

name: Paneer Tikka Masala
instructions: Marinate paneer cubes in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, garam masala, and salt for 30 minutes.
Grill or sauté paneer and bell peppers until lightly charred and set aside.
Heat butter and oil in a pan, sauté onions until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in tomato puree, cumin, coriander, and simmer until oil separates.
Add cream, kasuri methi, and cook for 2 minutes.
Add paneer and bell peppers to the sauce, simmer for 5 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro and serve hot.
cooking_tips: Char the paneer lightly for authentic tikka flavor.
Use fresh tomatoes or good-quality puree for the best sauce.
Kasuri methi adds a signature smoky aroma — don’t skip it.
serving_suggestions: Serve with naan, roti, or jeera rice.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for 2 days and reheat gently.

name: Vegetable Biryani
instructions: Wash and soak basmati rice for 30 minutes.
Heat oil and ghee in a pan, fry sliced onions until golden brown. Set aside half for garnish.
Add ginger-garlic paste, green chili, and sauté briefly.
Add chopped tomatoes, mixed vegetables, biryani masala, and yogurt. Cook until vegetables are soft.
Layer partially cooked rice over the vegetable mixture.
Sprinkle saffron milk, mint, cilantro, and fried onions.
Cover and cook on low heat for 20 minutes (dum cooking).
Gently fluff the biryani and serve hot.
cooking_tips: Parboil the rice until about 70% cooked.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot and seal the lid for dum cooking.
Brown onions slowly for the best flavor and texture.
serving_suggestions: Serve with raita, papad, and salad.
storage_tips: Store refrigerated for 2 days and reheat with a splash of water.

name: Rogan Josh
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot and sauté sliced onions until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add lamb pieces and brown on all sides.
Mix in yogurt, kashmiri chili powder, coriander, cumin, and salt.
Add whole spices: cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, and bay leaf.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until lamb is tender.
Adjust seasoning and cook uncovered for 5 minutes to thicken the gravy.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot.
cooking_tips: Cook on low heat to keep the lamb tender.
Kashmiri chili gives color without overwhelming heat.
Browning the lamb adds depth to the curry.
serving_suggestions: Serve with basmati rice or naan.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for 2 days. The flavors improve after resting.

name: Methi Chicken
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and sauté onions until translucent.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until fragrant.
Add chicken pieces and brown lightly on all sides.
Add tomatoes, green chili, turmeric, cumin, and coriander. Cook until tomatoes soften.
Stir in chopped fenugreek leaves and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add garam masala and cream, cook for another 5 minutes.
Adjust seasoning and garnish with fresh fenugreek or cilantro.
Serve hot with rice or roti.
cooking_tips: Use fresh methi leaves for the best aroma.
Simmer gently so the chicken stays tender.
Add cream at the end to keep the gravy rich and smooth.
serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed rice or paratha.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for 2 days and reheat gently.

name: Paneer Biryani
instructions: Soak basmati rice for 30 minutes and drain.
Heat oil and ghee in a large pan, fry sliced onions until deep golden and set aside half for garnish.
Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, yogurt, biryani masala, and cook until oil separates.
Stir in paneer cubes and cook for 5 minutes.
Layer half-cooked rice over the paneer mixture, sprinkle chopped mint, cilantro, saffron milk, and fried onions.
Cover tightly and cook on low heat for 20-25 minutes until rice finishes steaming.
Gently fluff the biryani, garnish with remaining fried onions, and serve hot.
cooking_tips: Parboil rice until about 70% cooked before layering.
Use a heavy pot and seal the lid well to trap steam for dum cooking.
Brown the onions slowly for the best flavor and texture.
serving_suggestions: Serve with raita and salad.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for 2 days and reheat with a splash of water.

name: Paneer Butter Masala
instructions: Heat oil and butter in a pan over medium heat.
Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger and garlic, cooking for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add tomatoes and cashews, then cook until the tomatoes become soft.
Allow the mixture to cool slightly and blend into a smooth puree.
Return the puree to the pan and cook for 5 minutes.
Add turmeric, coriander powder, red chili powder, garam masala and salt.
Add paneer cubes and simmer for 8–10 minutes.
Mix in fresh cream and crushed kasuri methi.
Cook for another 2 minutes and serve hot.
cooking_tips: Use fresh paneer for the softest texture.
Soak paneer cubes in warm water for 10 minutes before cooking.
Blend the gravy thoroughly for a smooth restaurant-style consistency.
serving_suggestions: Serve hot with butter naan, roti, jeera rice, or steamed basmati rice.
storage_tips: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently before serving.

name: Palak Paneer
instructions: Wash spinach thoroughly and blanch it in boiling water for 2 minutes.
Transfer the spinach immediately into ice-cold water to retain its green color.
Blend the spinach into a smooth puree.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté cumin until fragrant.
Add chopped onions and cook until golden.
Add ginger, garlic, and green chili, then sauté for 2 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft.
Mix in turmeric, garam masala, and salt.
Pour in the spinach puree and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add paneer cubes and cook for another 5 minutes.
Stir in fresh cream and cook for 2 more minutes before serving.
cooking_tips: Do not overcook the spinach to preserve its bright green color.
Soak paneer in warm water before adding it to keep it soft.
Add cream at the end for a richer texture.
serving_suggestions: Serve hot with naan, roti, paratha, or steamed basmati rice.
storage_tips: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat gently before serving.

name: Chole Masala
instructions: Soak chickpeas overnight and pressure cook until soft.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté cumin seeds.
Add chopped onions and cook until golden brown.
Add ginger, garlic, and green chili, then sauté for 2 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they become soft.
Mix in turmeric, coriander powder, red chili powder, garam masala, amchur powder, and salt.
Cook the masala until oil separates.
Add cooked chickpeas along with a little cooking water.
Simmer for 15 minutes so the flavors blend well.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot.
cooking_tips: Cook chickpeas until very soft for the best texture.
Mash a few chickpeas into the gravy to make it thicker.
A pinch of black tea while boiling chickpeas gives an authentic dark color.
serving_suggestions: Serve hot with bhature, poori, naan, roti, or steamed basmati rice.
storage_tips: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Rajma Masala
instructions: Soak kidney beans overnight and pressure cook until tender.
Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds until they splutter.
Add finely chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger, garlic, and green chili, cooking for 2 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft and the oil separates.
Mix in turmeric, coriander powder, red chili powder, garam masala, and salt.
Add the cooked kidney beans along with some of the cooking liquid.
Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Lightly mash a few beans to naturally thicken the gravy.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot.
cooking_tips: Always soak kidney beans overnight for even cooking.
Cook the gravy well before adding the beans for a richer flavor.
Slow simmering improves the taste and texture.
serving_suggestions: Serve hot with steamed basmati rice, jeera rice, roti, or naan.
storage_tips: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Dal Tadka
instructions: Wash the toor dal thoroughly and pressure cook it with turmeric and water until soft.
Mash the cooked dal lightly to obtain a smooth consistency.
Heat ghee in a pan and add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and a pinch of asafoetida.
Add chopped garlic and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger, green chili, and chopped onions, cooking until the onions become translucent.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they soften completely.
Mix in red chili powder, garam masala, and salt.
Pour the cooked dal into the pan and mix well.
Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, adding water if needed to adjust the consistency.
Garnish with freshly chopped coriander and serve hot.
cooking_tips: Use ghee instead of oil for authentic flavor.
Do not overcook the tempering, as burnt garlic can make the dal bitter.
Add a squeeze of lemon juice before serving for extra freshness.
serving_suggestions: Serve hot with steamed rice, jeera rice, roti, chapati, or naan. Pair with papad and pickle for a complete meal.
storage_tips: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat with a little water before serving.

name: Aloo Gobi
instructions: Wash and cut the potatoes and cauliflower into medium-sized pieces.
Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds until they begin to splutter.
Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger, garlic, and green chili, then cook for 2 minutes.
Mix in chopped tomatoes, turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook until the tomatoes become soft.
Add potatoes and cauliflower, stirring well to coat them with the masala.
Cover and cook on low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Sprinkle garam masala and garnish with fresh coriander before serving.
cooking_tips: Do not overcook the cauliflower to keep it slightly firm.
Add a tablespoon of water if the vegetables begin sticking to the pan.
Roast the vegetables for a smoky flavor.
serving_suggestions: Serve hot with roti, chapati, naan, or steamed basmati rice.
storage_tips: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat before serving.

name: Chole Masala
instructions: Soak chickpeas overnight and pressure cook until soft.
Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds.
Sauté chopped onions until golden brown.
Add ginger, garlic, and green chili. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, coriander powder, red chili powder, and salt. Cook until oil separates.
Add cooked chickpeas with a little cooking water and mix well.
Add chole masala and simmer for 15 minutes.
Sprinkle garam masala, garnish with fresh coriander, and serve hot.
cooking_tips: Overnight soaking gives softer chickpeas.
Mash a few chickpeas while cooking for a thicker gravy.
A tea bag while boiling chickpeas gives authentic dark color.
serving_suggestions: Serve with bhature, puri, naan, jeera rice, or steamed rice along with sliced onions and lemon.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Rajma Masala
instructions: Soak kidney beans overnight and pressure cook until soft.
Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds.
Sauté chopped onions until golden brown.
Add ginger, garlic, and green chili, then cook for 2 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, coriander powder, red chili powder, and salt. Cook until the tomatoes become soft.
Add cooked kidney beans with some cooking liquid and mix well.
Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes until the gravy thickens.
Sprinkle garam masala, garnish with fresh coriander, and serve hot.
cooking_tips: Slow simmering enhances the flavor.
Mash a few kidney beans for a naturally thick gravy.
Freshly ground spices provide the best taste.
serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed basmati rice, jeera rice, chapati, or naan along with sliced onions and lemon wedges.
storage_tips: Store in the refrigerator for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Malai Kofta
instructions: Boil and mash the potatoes in a mixing bowl.
Add grated paneer, corn flour, salt, chopped cashews, and raisins. Mix well.
Shape the mixture into small round koftas.
Deep fry the koftas until golden brown and keep them aside.
Heat oil in another pan and sauté chopped onions until golden.
Add ginger, garlic, and tomatoes, then cook until soft.
Blend the mixture into a smooth gravy.
Return the gravy to the pan and add turmeric, coriander powder, red chili powder, garam masala, cashew paste, and cream.
Simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the fried koftas just before serving.
Garnish with fresh coriander and a drizzle of cream.
cooking_tips: Add the koftas only before serving to keep them crispy.
Use fresh paneer for a softer texture.
Blend the gravy until completely smooth for a restaurant-style finish.
serving_suggestions: Serve hot with butter naan, garlic naan, tandoori roti, or jeera rice.
storage_tips: Store the gravy and koftas separately in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Combine only while reheating.

name: Chicken Biryani
instructions: Wash and soak basmati rice for 30 minutes.
Marinate the chicken with yogurt, turmeric, red chili powder, biryani masala, ginger-garlic paste, and salt for at least 1 hour.
Cook the rice until it is about 70% done and drain.
Heat oil and ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Fry sliced onions until golden brown and reserve some for garnish.
Cook the marinated chicken until it is nearly done.
Add chopped tomatoes, mint leaves, and coriander leaves.
Layer the partially cooked rice over the chicken mixture.
Sprinkle fried onions, garam masala, mint, and coriander between the layers.
Cover the pot tightly and cook on low heat (dum) for 20 minutes.
Allow the biryani to rest for 10 minutes before gently mixing and serving.
cooking_tips: Use aged basmati rice for the best aroma and texture.
Do not overcook the rice before layering.
Marinating the chicken overnight enhances the flavor.
serving_suggestions: Serve hot with onion raita, boiled egg, pickle, and papad.
storage_tips: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat with a sprinkle of water before serving.

name: Hyderabadi Dum Biryani
instructions: Wash and soak the basmati rice for 30 minutes.
Marinate the chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, biryani masala, turmeric, red chili powder, salt, mint, coriander, and fried onions for at least 2 hours.
Cook the rice until it is about 70% cooked and drain.
Grease a heavy-bottomed pot with ghee.
Spread the marinated chicken evenly at the bottom of the pot.
Layer the partially cooked rice over the chicken.
Sprinkle saffron milk, fried onions, mint leaves, coriander leaves, and ghee over the rice.
Seal the pot with a tight-fitting lid or dough.
Cook on very low heat for 35–40 minutes.
Allow the biryani to rest for 10 minutes before gently mixing and serving.
cooking_tips: Marinate the chicken overnight for maximum flavor.
Use high-quality aged basmati rice.
Cook on low heat to prevent the rice from burning.
Do not stir while the biryani is cooking.
serving_suggestions: Serve with mirchi ka salan, onion raita, boiled eggs, pickle, and fresh salad.
storage_tips: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat with a little water to maintain moisture.

name: Kadai Paneer
instructions: Dry roast coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and dried red chilies, then grind them into a coarse powder.
Heat oil in a kadai or deep pan.
Sauté chopped onions until lightly golden.
Add ginger, garlic, and green chili, then cook for 2 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft.
Mix in turmeric, freshly ground kadai masala, garam masala, and salt.
Add chopped capsicum and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until slightly tender.
Add paneer cubes and mix gently.
Sprinkle crushed kasuri methi and cook for another 2 minutes.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot.
cooking_tips: Freshly ground kadai masala gives the best flavor.
Do not overcook the capsicum so it stays slightly crunchy.
Add paneer at the end to keep it soft.
serving_suggestions: Serve hot with butter naan, roti, laccha paratha, or jeera rice.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for up to 3 days in an airtight container. Reheat on low heat before serving.

name: Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: Cook spaghetti in well-salted boiling water until al dente.
In a bowl, whisk together eggs and grated Parmesan cheese. Season with black pepper.
Fry pancetta with garlic in a pan over medium heat until crispy.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta cooking water before draining.
Remove pan from heat. Add drained pasta to the pancetta.
Quickly pour the egg-cheese mixture over pasta, tossing continuously.
Add pasta water a little at a time to create a creamy sauce.
Serve immediately with extra Parmesan and black pepper.
cooking_tips: Never add cream — the creaminess comes from eggs and pasta water.
Remove the pan from heat before adding eggs to prevent scrambling.
Use guanciale (cured pork cheek) for the most authentic version.
serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with extra Parmesan and a simple green salad.
storage_tips: Best eaten fresh. Can be refrigerated for 1 day but sauce may dry out.

name: Margherita Pizza
instructions: Preheat oven to 250°C (480°F) with a pizza stone or baking sheet inside.
Stretch pizza dough on a floured surface to desired thickness.
Spread tomato sauce evenly, leaving a border for the crust.
Tear mozzarella and distribute over the sauce.
Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt.
Bake for 12-15 minutes until crust is golden and cheese is bubbly.
Remove from oven and immediately top with fresh basil leaves.
Drizzle with more olive oil and serve immediately.
cooking_tips: A very hot oven is key to a good pizza crust.
Don't overload with toppings — less is more for Margherita.
Add fresh basil after baking to preserve its flavor.
serving_suggestions: Serve hot, cut into slices. Pair with a simple arugula salad.
storage_tips: Best eaten fresh. Reheat in oven at 200°C for 5 minutes.

substitutions.pizza dough: flatbread or tortilla for quick version

name: Risotto ai Funghi
instructions: Heat vegetable broth in a saucepan and keep warm.
Sauté mushrooms in olive oil until golden. Season and set aside.
In another pan, sweat onions and garlic in butter until soft.
Add arborio rice and toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in white wine and stir until absorbed.
Add warm broth one ladle at a time, stirring constantly until absorbed.
Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Stir in mushrooms, Parmesan, and remaining butter. Season to taste.
cooking_tips: Never stop stirring — it releases the starch that makes risotto creamy.
Add broth warm, not cold.
The final addition of butter and cheese (mantecatura) is what makes it silky.
serving_suggestions: Serve immediately in warmed bowls. Garnish with truffle oil for luxury.
storage_tips: Risotto doesn't store well. Best made and eaten immediately.

name: Chicken Piccata
instructions: Pound chicken breasts thin between plastic wrap.
Season with salt and pepper and dredge in flour, shake off excess.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook chicken 3 minutes per side until golden. Transfer to plate.
In the same pan, sauté garlic briefly.
Add white wine and chicken broth, scraping up any brown bits.
Add lemon juice, capers, and butter. Simmer until sauce thickens.
Return chicken to sauce, simmer 2 minutes, garnish with parsley.
cooking_tips: Pounding chicken ensures even cooking.
Don't skip the flour — it helps create the sauce.
Use fresh lemon juice for bright, fresh flavor.
serving_suggestions: Serve over angel hair pasta or with roasted vegetables.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat gently to avoid drying out.

name: Penne Arrabbiata
instructions: Cook penne in salted boiling water until al dente.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add sliced garlic and red chili flakes. Cook until garlic is fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, salt, and a pinch of sugar.
Simmer sauce for 15 minutes until thickened.
Toss drained pasta with the sauce.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve hot.
cooking_tips: Arrabbiata means 'angry' in Italian — make it as spicy as you like.
Save pasta water to adjust sauce consistency.
Use San Marzano tomatoes for best flavor.
serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread and a green salad.
storage_tips: Sauce keeps for 3 days. Cook pasta fresh when serving.
